 About 11,000 HAIARA power banks sold on Amazon.com are being recalled because the lithium battery can explode and ignite, creating fire and burn hazards, according to the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission.
 The recalled power banks are model W5 PRO, sold by Mitrytech on Amazon from May 2025 through September 2026 for between $18 and $22. The black power banks have “20W” printed on the front and “Model: W5 PRO” on the side. The recall applies to units with no date code, formatted as YYYYMMDD, printed on the side.
 READ MORE | Caught on camera: E-bike battery explosion engulfs Troutdale home 
 Mitrytech has received 600 reports of fires and other thermal incidents, including three reports of burn injuries and nine reports of property damage.
 Consumers should stop using the power banks immediately. People who bought one from Mitrytech on Amazon should contact the company at HAIARArecall@outlook.com or visit haiara.net/recalls.html for refund instructions. Consumers will need to submit a photo of the power bank marked “recalled” and confirm they disposed of it according to applicable laws and regulations.
